New data — staged parameter estimation

Generated 2026-09-29 10:24 with GrowthParameterEstimation.run_joint_fit on the Mean Cells trajectories in New Datasets. Two model families are compared: one population per line (candidates from the Candidate models page), and healthy / damaged two-population models (see below). At each stage every candidate is fitted, all are ranked together by BIC, and the optimal (lowest-BIC) model is reported.

  • Stage 1 · Untreated monocultures (A2780 = sensitive N, A2780cis = resistant C) → growth rate r and carrying capacity K per line.
  • Stage 1b · Low-resource monocultures (30k sheets): inherit r and K; fit the low-resource terms.
  • Stage 2 · Treated monocultures: inherit r and K; the three doses of each line are fitted jointly with shared drug parameters; EC50 is fixed at 1 µM.
  • Stage 3 · Untreated (Ce0) and treated (Ce1) cocultures together: all three seeding ratios and both conditions (12 trajectories) are fitted at once with one shared carrying capacity K; Ce1 is 1 µM cisplatin.
  • Stage 3b · Low-resource cocultures (30k, runs 1 and 2): inherit K and α from Stage 3 and d^LR from Stage 1b.

How to compare models: each fit shows a BIC chart and a comparison table for all candidates. Below them, the Show fit for buttons switch the plot, the fitted equation (with the estimated values substituted) and the parameter table to any candidate; All candidates overlaid draws every candidate on one plot. ΔBIC evidence bands: < 2 weak, 2–6 positive, 6–10 strong, > 10 very strong.

Low-resource data: only A2780 / A2780cis 30k sheets from ALL A2780-cis LR data.xlsx are used (Tyknu is not). FBS is 10% in normal medium (\(u_R = 0\), so Stages 1–3 have no low-resource term) and 0.5% in low resource, so \(u_R = (10-0.5)/(10-0.05) = 0.9548\) in Stages 1b and 3b. Sudden transient drops are excluded from the fit (a point below half of the previous kept value, by more than 50 cells, after which the trajectory recovers to at least 80% of that value; steady declines and spikes are kept), as are values that exactly repeat an earlier day's value (copy/paste errors); each excluded point is drawn as a grey × and replaced by a hollow diamond placed on the fitted line afterwards. All excluded points are listed at the end. Doses are read from the file names: IC25 file = 1.47 µM, IC50 file = 1 µM, IC75 file = 0.62 µM. Points are observations; lines are model fits. All plots share the same axes (0–14 days, 0–4800 cells).

Optimal model at each stage

Optimal = lowest BIC among every candidate of both model families. Asymmetric models (different parameters for the sensitive and resistant line, \(\alpha_{NC} \ne \alpha_{CN}\)) are allowed throughout. ± values are 95% intervals (1.96 × asymptotic SE; residuals of mean trajectories are correlated, so treat them as lower bounds). The last column gives the best model of the other family and how much worse its BIC is.

Healthy / damaged two-population models

A second model family, fitted alongside the one-population-per-line models at Stages 1b, 2, 3 and 3b. Each line X (N = A2780 naive/sensitive, C = A2780cis resistant) is split into healthy cells \(X_H\), which divide, and damaged cells \(X_D\), which no longer divide but still take up space and are still counted. A stress (cisplatin at Stages 2 and 3, low resource at Stages 1b and 3b) damages healthy cells at rate \(k_X\). Damaged cells either die at rate \(\delta_X\) or are repaired back to the healthy pool at rate \(\rho_X\):

\[\frac{dX_H}{dt}=r_X X_H\left(1-\frac{X+\alpha_{XY}Y}{K}\right)-k_X X_H+\rho_X X_D,\qquad \frac{dX_D}{dt}=k_X X_H-(\rho_X+\delta_X)X_D,\qquad X=X_H+X_D\]
\[k_X=\kappa_X H_X(D)\ \text{(cisplatin; } H_X=\tfrac{D^{h_X}}{1+D^{h_X}}\text{ or } D\text{)},\qquad k_X=\sigma_X u_R\ \text{(low resource)}\]

Variants: irreversible (\(\rho = 0\)); repair (\(\rho > 0\)); two- or four-step transit (damaged cells pass \(X_{D1}\to X_{D2}\to\dots\) at rate \(\delta\) before dying, a longer and more peaked delay); for low resource, arrest without death (\(\delta = 0\), damaged = quiescent) and crowding-dependent damage or arrest (rate \(\sigma_X u_R\,g_X\), \(g_X = (X+\alpha Y)/K\), as in Gyllenberg & Webb); for cisplatin, damage that builds up at rate \(\lambda\) (\(k_X = \kappa_X H_X(D)(1-e^{-\lambda_X t})\)); and, in coculture, coculture damage \(b_N\) of sensitive cells in both Ce0 and Ce1. Every rate is separate for N and C (asymmetric).

No explicit time dependence is needed: for a dose switched on at day 0, \(H_X(D)(1-e^{-\lambda_X t})\) is exactly the state \(E_X\) of an effect compartment \(dE_X/dt = \lambda_X\,(H_X(D) - E_X)\), \(E_X(0)=0\). Written that way, every healthy / damaged model here is autonomous and can be driven by any dose schedule \(D(t)\) (optimal control); the fits are identical.

Carried forward within this family: the Stage 2 winner's damage structure and \(\kappa, h, \delta, \rho\) go to Stage 3; the Stage 1b winner's \(\sigma, \delta, \rho\) and the Stage 3 winner's \(K, \alpha\) go to Stage 3b. The one-population family keeps its own chain as before.

Literature basis. Proliferating and damaged (non-dividing, dying) compartments with transit through damage stages: Simeoni et al. 2004 (Cancer Res 64:1094) and the in-vitro transit-compartment model of Lobo & Balthasar 2002 (AAPS PharmSci 4:E42). Repair of cisplatin–DNA lesions, faster in cisplatin-resistant A2780 derivatives, which motivates a separate \(\rho_C\): Masuda et al. 1988 (Cancer Res 48:5713) and Parker et al. 1991 (J Clin Invest 87:772), which also reports lower platinum uptake (a lower \(\kappa_C\)). Reversible switching between proliferating and quiescent cells under nutrient limitation: Gyllenberg & Webb 1989 (Growth Dev Aging 53:25).

Stage 1 — Untreated monoculture

\[\text{Logistic ★:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)\]
\[\text{Theta logistic:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left[1-\left(\frac{X}{K_X}\right)^{\theta_X}\right]\]
\[\text{Gompertz:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\log\left(\frac{K_X}{X}\right)\]

Each cell line is fitted separately. Carried forward: the logistic \(r_X, K_X\).

Stage 1b — Low-resource monoculture

\[\text{Lineage-specific subtractive loss ★:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)-d_X^{LR}\,u_R(t)\,X,\qquad u_R=\frac{10-F}{10-0.05}\]
\[\text{Growth-rate and carrying-capacity modifiers:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=\rho_r r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{\rho_K K_X}\right)\]
\[\text{Separately fitted growth rate:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X^{LR} X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)\]
\[\text{Accumulated damage, 4 steps (delayed loss):}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)-d_X^{LR}\,u_R\,A_4(t)\,X,\qquad A_n(t)=1-e^{-\lambda_X^{LR} t}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\frac{(\lambda_X^{LR} t)^k}{k!}\]
\[\text{Immediate loss + accumulated damage, } n = 4 \text{ or } 8:\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)-\left(d_X^{LR}+d_X^{acc}A_n(t)\right)u_R\,X\]

Accumulated damage: cells pass through \(n\) damage steps at rate \(\lambda\) before the extra loss acts (mean delay \(n/\lambda\)), the transit-compartment idea used for delayed drug effects (Lobo & Balthasar 2002; Simeoni et al. 2004).

\(r_X, K_X\) are inherited from Stage 1. Sheets: 1 - mono A2780 30k and 1 - mono A2780cis 30k. Carried forward: \(d_X^{LR}\) from the ★ model.

Stage 2 — Treated monoculture

\[A_X(t)=1-e^{-\lambda_X t},\qquad H_X(D)=\frac{D^{h_X}}{EC_{50}^{h_X}+D^{h_X}},\qquad EC_{50}=1\ \mu\text{M (fixed)}\]
\[\text{Time-delayed Hill ★:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)-\beta_X A_X(t) H_X(D) X\]
\[\text{No Hill saturation:}\quad \frac{dX}{dt}=r_X X\left(1-\frac{X}{K_X}\right)-\beta_X A_X(t)\, D\, X\]

\(r_X, K_X\) are fixed from Stage 1. Free: \(\beta_X, \lambda_X\) (and \(h_X\) for the Hill model), shared across 0.62, 1.0 and 1.47 µM. The "distributed" form on the Candidate models page, \(r_X X - \tfrac{r_X}{K_X}X^2 - \beta_X A_X H_X X\), is the same equation expanded, so it is not fitted separately. Carried forward: \(\lambda_X\) and \(h_X\).

Stage 3 — Untreated + treated coculture, shared carrying capacity

\[\frac{dN}{dt}=r_N N\left(1-\frac{N+\alpha_{NC}C}{K}\right)-d_N N-\mathbb{1}_{\text{Ce1}}\,\beta_N A_N(t) H_N(D) N\]
\[\frac{dC}{dt}=r_C C\left(1-\frac{C+\alpha_{CN}N}{K}\right)-d_C C-\mathbb{1}_{\text{Ce1}}\,\beta_C A_C(t) H_C(D) C\]

N = A2780 (sensitive), C = A2780cis (resistant). K is one parameter shared by both lineages, all three ratios and both conditions. Candidates switch terms on and off: one-for-one (\(\alpha_{NC}=\alpha_{CN}=1\)) or asymmetric crowding; treatment \(\beta, \lambda, h\) inherited from Stage 2 or \(\beta\) refitted; death terms on neither, the sensitive line only, or both lines; a kill term on the resistant line or not. The kill term acts only on Ce1 (D = 1 µM). Parameter tables give asymptotic standard errors and 95% intervals; because consecutive points of a mean trajectory are correlated, treat them as lower bounds on the true uncertainty.

Inherited: r_N = 0.8187, r_C = 0.5807 (Stage 1); λ_N = 0.1582, λ_C = 0.1812, H_N(1 µM) = 0.500, H_C(1 µM) = 1.000 (Stage 2). With D = EC50 = 1 µM the Hill factor is exactly 0.5 whatever h is, so \(h\) cannot be re-estimated from the coculture data.
